commit.message: docs: add release notes

chainntnfs: add an asynchronous notifier state machine model

The existing model completes every historical scan inside its
registration and gives every subscriber the same height hint, so the
earlier hint bugs fixed in the previous commits weren't reachable from
it.

In this commit, we add a rapid state machine that queues historical
scans and completes, fails, or reports Neutrino progress for them in
any order relative to registrations, blocks, bounded reorgs, and
restarts that re-register subscribers in a random order. Subscribers
draw their own hints, which can be earlier than a prior subscriber's or
later than the event itself, and the model covers spends alongside
confirmations.

Instead of predicting each notification, the oracle checks invariants
after every action: no subscriber receives an event that isn't in the
chain, a subscriber whose hint precedes its event is notified once all
scans for it have reported, and the hint cache never lets such a
subscriber skip its event if it registered first after a restart.
Reverting the prefix scans for either kind, the pending scan
accounting, or hint origins makes the model fail within a few thousand
runs.

chainntnfs: scan uncovered prefixes for earlier height hints

Duplicate confirmation and spend registrations for the same request
share a single historical scan. If a later subscriber supplied an
earlier height hint than the one the scan started from, it just waited
on that scan, so a confirmation or spend below the first subscriber's
hint was never found.

In this commit, we track how far down each set's coverage reaches, and
a later subscriber whose hint is below it gets a supplemental scan of
only the uncovered prefix. The set counts its pending scans, so an
empty result from one scan can't advance the shared hint while another
is still checking an earlier range. The persisted hint needs no change
when a prefix is dispatched: its origin is above the new subscriber's
hint, so a restart before the prefix completes scans it again.

Supplemental dispatches are flagged explicitly, and Neutrino only
extends a dispatch's end height to its own tip for an initial scan, so
a prefix scan keeps its fixed boundary. A prefix also never ends above
the notifier's tip: after a reorg, the blocks above it are connected
again and seen at tip, and a backend can't scan blocks it doesn't have
yet. A backend that fails a scan
never reports it, which leaves the set pending and its hint frozen,
failing safe until a restart scans the range again.

multi: persist the scan origin of cached height hints

A cached height hint only records where the next historical scan should
begin, not where the scans that produced it started. So if a subscriber
with a hint later than the actual confirmation or spend is the one
watching a request, its scans never cover that block, yet the hint it
leaves behind is trusted by the next registration. After a restart, a
subscriber with an earlier, correct hint that registers first then
skips straight past its event.

In this commit, we store a HeightHint of both the height and its origin,
and a cached hint is only used by a registration whose own hint is at
or above that origin. Otherwise, the scan starts at the subscriber's
hint. Each set tracks the coverage its hints are persisted with, and
Neutrino tags its incremental spend progress with the scan's origin.
We also query the cache under the notifier's lock, so updateHints can't
change the hint between the read and the set being created.

In channeldb, the hint is encoded as its height followed by its origin.
A legacy four byte value decodes with an unknown origin, which we trust
only for the first subscriber, same as before, so no migration is
needed. The height comes first, so an older binary reading the value
still recovers it. The cache interfaces now take a map of hints so each
request keeps its own origin while updateHints still writes every hint
in a single transaction.

channeldb: persist local updates the peer acked before our first revoke (#11268)

* channeldb: persist local updates the peer acked before our first revoke

In this commit, we fix AdvanceCommitChainTail so it always persists our
updates the peer acknowledged but hasn't signed for yet. It used to
return early when no unsigned acked updates were stored, which skipped
that write. Nothing stores the unsigned acked updates until we first
revoke a commitment of our own, so every channel takes that path until
then, not only nodes that are upgrading, as the comment assumed.

The window matters for fee updates. If the initiator's first update is a
fee update, the peer revokes, and the connection drops before the peer's
commitment_signed arrives, the initiator restores without the fee update.
It then rejects the peer's valid signature for a commitment that covers
the fee, and the link force closes the channel. The new test runs that
sequence, and fails without the fix.

Settles and fails can't hit this, since removing an HTLC needs it locked
in, which means we already revoked once. The mirror test's restart step
found this.

* docs: add release note for the unsigned acked updates fix

commit.message:
lncli: only update the policy fields that are passed

updatechanpolicy no longer requires base_fee_msat, fee_rate and
time_lock_delta on every call; fields that aren't passed keep their
current value. The flags are now string flags parsed explicitly, which
removes the misleading "(default: 0)" from the help text and rejects
invalid input instead of treating it as zero.

Individual fields are set with the flags. Positional arguments are only
accepted when all three fields are set, since it's otherwise ambiguous
which field a value fills. A trailing channel point is recognised by its
colon, so it's never read as a policy field, and any argument left over
after the policy values and one channel point is rejected.

An lnd that predates partial updates would reset an omitted fee to zero,
so lncli checks the version first and refuses such an update.

Fixes #1523.

commit.message:
rpcserver: support partial channel policy updates

Move the request validation and conversion of UpdateChannelPolicy into
channelPolicyFromRequest and honor partial_update there. Non-zero values
for fields not marked in partial_update are rejected rather than
silently ignored.

commit.message:
multi: allow a policy update to keep existing fields

Turn BaseFee, FeeRate and TimeLockDelta of ChannelPolicy into options,
so the local channel manager leaves the matching fields of the current
edge untouched when they're empty. UpdateChannelPolicy keeps setting all
three.

commit.message:
lnrpc: add partial_update to PolicyUpdateRequest

PolicyUpdateRequest can't tell an unset base fee, fee rate or time lock
delta from zero, so every update has to send all three. Add an opt-in
partial_update message that marks which of the three fields to apply,
so callers can update individual fields. Without partial_update the
existing semantics are unchanged, as current clients rely on omitted
(zero) values being applied.

Fixes #1523.
